episode_title: The Science of SaaS Pricing, Packaging, and Willingness to Pay
summary: Patrick Campbell explains why monetization has 4x the bottom-line leverage of acquisition, how to identify your true value metric, why discounting destroys customer LTV, and the Van Westendorp Price Sensitivity meter.
transcript:
Lenny Rachitsky: Patrick, welcome. At ProfitWell, you analyzed pricing data from over 30,000 subscription companies. You found that improving pricing yields four times more revenue growth than improving acquisition. Why is monetization so neglected by product teams?

Patrick Campbell: Hey Lenny. It's neglected because changing prices causes emotional panic. Product teams think: 'If we raise our price, our existing users will revolt on Twitter, and churn will spike.' So they spend 99% of their waking hours optimizing acquisition funnels.

Our benchmark data showed that a 1% improvement in customer acquisition yields roughly a 3.2% increase in bottom-line growth. But a 1% improvement in monetization—meaning pricing and packaging—yields an 11.1% increase in bottom-line impact. Monetization is four times more efficient than acquisition because every dollar flows directly to gross margin without incremental CAC.

Lenny Rachitsky: What is the single most important rule when designing SaaS pricing tiers?

Patrick Campbell: Your Value Metric. A value metric is what you charge per—per seat, per gigabyte, per email sent, per transaction volume. 80% of SaaS companies make the mistake of charging purely per seat. But per-seat pricing penalizes collaboration! If five people on a team want to collaborate on a design file, charging per seat makes the buyer restrict licenses, which kills your product's viral expansion loop.

The holy grail is finding a value metric that directly scales with the value the customer receives. For HubSpot, it was number of marketing contacts. For Zapier, it is number of task executions. When your customer grows, your revenue grows automatically, without having to renegotiate contracts every quarter.
